statement: Personal data is erased, and the parties processing it for the organization erase it, once its purpose is served, consent is withdrawn or erasure is requested, unless a legal ground to keep it applies. Automated or systematic erasure runs on those triggers, and processors are told to erase whatever was made available to them. Where the organization is a large e-commerce, social media or online gaming intermediary of the kind the law names, a user's data is also erased after three years without contact, and the data principal is warned at least 48 hours before. Proof is erasure job logs, erasure records and the request log.
why_asked: Personal data is kept after its purpose ends and survives in processor systems, and each retained record is a breach waiting to happen.
how_to_ask: Ask what triggers erasure, who confirms it happened and how processors are told. Trace a recent erasure request from receipt to closure. Example probe: "Show me the last erasure request, the proof the data is gone and the instruction sent to the processor."
question: Does your organization make sure personal data is erased, including at its processors, once its purpose is served, consent is withdrawn or erasure is requested?
expected_evidence: Erasure procedure with triggers; erasure job logs or erasure records; rights request log with closure evidence; processor erasure instructions; inactivity erasure warning template where applicable, for the audit period.
good_looks_like: Erasure triggers are defined and run automatically or by a controlled procedure. Processors receive erasure instructions and confirm them. Each erasure request closes with proof of erasure or a recorded legal ground to keep the data.
test: Sample personal data records past their erasure trigger and sample erasure requests from the audit period. Trace each to erasure logs or a recorded legal ground, including at processors. Where the inactivity rule applies, check one erased account had a warning at least 48 hours before. Pass if every sampled item was erased or has a recorded legal ground.
baseline_risk: Personal data lingers past its purpose, in the organization and at processors, and erasure duties are missed.
key_settings: dpdpa: where the organization is a named large e-commerce, social media or online gaming intermediary, erase a user's data after three years without contact | dpdpa: warn the data principal at least 48 hours before inactivity erasure | dpdpa: thresholds are 2 crore registered users in India for e-commerce and social media, 50 lakh for online gaming

statement: A documented retention schedule sets, for each category of personal data and each purpose, a retention period or an erasure trigger. Where the schedule keeps data beyond its purpose, it names the law that requires it. Retention and deletion settings on systems holding personal data are checked on a defined cycle to match the schedule. Proof is the schedule and the system setting checks.
why_asked: Without a schedule that names a reason for every retention, data is kept by default and nobody can defend why.
how_to_ask: Ask for the schedule and pick a few data categories. Check each has a period or trigger and a stated reason, then check the system setting. Example probe: "Take your customer contact data. What is its retention period and what law or purpose backs that?"
question: Does your organization maintain a retention schedule for personal data that names the legal ground for any retention beyond the purpose?
expected_evidence: Retention schedule by data category and purpose; legal ground references; system configuration screenshots; schedule-versus-settings check records, for the audit period.
good_looks_like: Every data category and purpose has a period or erasure trigger. Any retention beyond the purpose names its legal ground. Settings on sampled systems match the schedule, and mismatches are fixed.
test: Read the schedule. Sample data categories and check each has a period or trigger and a named law where data is kept beyond its purpose. Compare retention or deletion settings on the systems holding them. Pass if every sampled category is scheduled and settings match.
baseline_risk: Data is kept without a recorded reason or deleted too early or too late because systems do not follow any schedule.
